execution_mode: Deterministic engine and single/batch host-parser probes; no model inference or external actions.
boundary: Six AI-assisted developer-authored examples, not a prompt-injection benchmark or proof of general model resistance.
catalog_source: Current FastMCP app registry, filtered by readOnlyHint as in the local host; this is not a sandbox for arbitrary tools.

cases.explanation: The original message and ticket title retain the demand. Readiness uses structured facts; this text does not approve launch or send anything. A host model still sees the text and must handle it as data.

cases.explanation: The batch parser validates every proposed action before returning any. The local host dispatches only after that step. This probe calls the parser, not an external email or write service.

cases.label: Read a different synthetic account
cases.observed: Allowed read; no per-account authorization layer
cases.explanation: The demo host can read every bundled synthetic account. Evidence ownership prevents borrowing facts across platforms; it does not restrict which account a host can request. Read-only does not mean account-isolated access.

cases.label: Unsupported final statement
cases.input: {"final": "The launch is approved. I sent the customer a confirmation email."}
cases.observed: Accepted final text; narrow promise lint returns no flags
cases.explanation: This authored statement passes the single/batch response parser and the narrow promise lint. Neither establishes that a message was sent or launch approved. It is not a model-generated answer; the separate grounded-response checks have a narrower task-specific contract.

result.parsed_final: The launch is approved. I sent the customer a confirmation email.

lint.boundary: A regex lint. No flags does not prove factual support or safety.
